messages:
anya: Quick RFC follow-up on enrichment fallback semantics — when an attribute lookup (tenant/billing key/service id) misses, do we: 1) fallthrough to heuristic attribution, or 2) emit a pending marker and attempt late/backfill? Need tradeoffs and a rollout proposal.

mike: Short take: heuristics reduce immediate latency but corrupt cost buckets and increase cardinality. Not great for billing accuracy.

leo: +1 to mike. Heuristics by host/route are brittle for multi-tenant infra. Prefer pending + backfill for keys that drive billing.

anya: Ops constraints: we can't block request paths on enrichment, and dashboards explode if too many pendings persist.

leo: Proposed hybrid: on miss emit envelope with "enrichment_status:pending" and "tenant:pending" and enqueue a lightweight enrichment_ticket to a side-channel. Aggregator treats pending as temporary tombstone for a short TTL (30s). If enrichment resolves within TTL emit a correction event; otherwise mark as unknown.

Example event (as a single-line JSON inside message): ```{"req_id":"r-11a","tenant":"pending","enrichment_status":"pending","ticket":"E-2024","ts":4791122334}```

tanya: Two asks: 1) storage and retention overhead for pending/correction flows, 2) compaction policy for corrections so we don't keep N correction rows forever. Also SRE: can the side-channel handle N QPS?

mike: Add enrichment_status tag values: hit, miss, pending, backfilled, corrected. Instrument miss-rate, pending-latency-p50/p90, correction-success-rate, and cardinality-impact. Billing: only attribute when enrichment_status in [hit, corrected, backfilled_success].

ingest-bot: Created ticket E-2024 for "enrichment-fallback-experiment" assigned to @leo and @anya — https://go/repo/issue/E-2024 :white_check_mark:

leo: Implementation plan: emit pending + ticket on miss; aggregator holds pending with TTL=30s; on correction emit idempotent correction events that carry old->new mapping so aggregator can apply delta. We'll include idempotency keys.

tanya: Rollout: 5% canary for 48h measuring: extra latency, change in dashboard cardinality/noise, and billing attribution delta. If correction success > 85% and cardinality increase < 10% then expand.

anya: I'll author a short RFC with schema examples, metric names, and ramp plan. Will cc SRE for throughput/retention numbers.

mike: Make sure correction events include dedupe keys and retention TTLs so aggregator compaction can prune old corrections.

anya: Great. Next: leo + mike to run a small sim and cost estimate, then we land RFC. Thanks everyone.
